To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
novH gene expression is regulated by WT1 and this regulation may play an important role in normal nephrogenesis and in the development of Wilms' tumor.

(i) novH is a novel type of IGFBP, (ii) WT1 represses the novH promoter, (iii) novH protein levels are reduced in cells transfected with WT1 and (iv) novH expression is inversely correlated to WT1 expression in Wilms' tumors.

(i) WT1 represses novH transcriptional activity; (ii) novH repression is mediated by both the zinc finger and the NH2-terminal repression domains of WT1; and (iii) WT1 repressor activity is not mediated by direct binding of WT1 to the novH promoter.

the regulation of nov expression and the potential role of nov in nephrogenic development.
the molecular basis of the development of the kidney and the mechanisms involved in the development of Wilms' tumor.
